literal: Ang inyong buwanang hulog para sa patakaran ng seguro ay dapat bayaran.
localized: Yung monthly premium ng LifeSecure policy n'yo na ₱2,450.00 ay due na sa October 15.
why: Filipino insurance customers say 'premium', 'policy' and 'due' in English even mid-Tagalog; machine-translated 'patakaran ng seguro' sounds bureaucratic. Taglish is the default variant; pure Tagalog is used only when the caller speaks it.

literal: ika-15 ng Oktubre, dalawang libo apat na raan at limampung piso
localized: Taglish/English: 'October 15', '₱2,450.00' (spoken '2,450 pesos'); formal Tagalog variant only: 'ika-15 ng Oktubre'
why: Everyday speech uses English month names and English numbers for money; Tagalog number words for amounts are rarely used and slow down a call.

localized: Makakapagbayad po ba kayo on or before the due date?
why: Customer-service register requires 'po' and the plural-respectful 'kayo/ninyo' instead of 'mo/ikaw', and addresses the customer as 'Ma'am Maria'.

literal: Kung hindi ka magbabayad, ang iyong polisiya ay mawawalan ng bisa.
localized: Gets ko po, Ma'am, mahirap talaga pag gipit. Para tuloy-tuloy pa rin ang coverage ng family n'yo, may 31-day grace period pa po kayo…
why: Empathy first ('gipit' = financially tight), frames the payment around the family/beneficiary, uses the real grace-period rule instead of a threat.

localized: Formal: 'angsuran ke-10 pembiayaan motor Bapak sebesar Rp1.250.000 akan jatuh tempo pada 15 Oktober 2026.' Casual: 'cicilan motor yang ke-10, Rp1.250.000, jatuh temponya tanggal 15.'
why: 'Anda' is stiff on a phone call; customers are addressed as Bapak/Pak. Formal callers get 'angsuran … sebesar'; casual callers get 'cicilan … jatuh temponya tanggal 15' while the bot stays polite (never 'lo/gue').

localized: Text 'Rp1.250.000' (dot thousands); TTS 'satu juta dua ratus lima puluh ribu rupiah'; penalty '0,5%' → 'nol koma lima persen'
why: Indonesian uses '.' for thousands and ',' for decimals; TTS engines misread 'Rp' and digits, so amounts are converted to words before synthesis.

literal: Anda harus membayar sekarang atau akan dikenakan denda.
localized: Saya ngerti, Pak, lagi berat ya. Biar nggak kena denda, usahakan bayar sebelum tanggal 15. Kalau butuh keringanan atau reschedule, harus lewat petugas kami.
why: Indonesian collection calls must avoid pressure (OJK consumer-protection rules); the bot acknowledges hardship, states the penalty factually and routes 'keringanan/restrukturisasi' to a human instead of promising it.

localized: Javanese ngoko ('durung ono duit', 'mengko tak bayar') → casual reply with 'nggih'; krama ('sampun kulo bayar') → formal reply; Sundanese ('teu acan aya artos, atuh') and Medan ('kek mana, awak belum gajian, lae') recognised as payment-difficulty / no-money objections
why: Regional vocabulary is in the intent examples and lexicons, so non-Jakarta speakers are understood and answered in standard polite Indonesian rather than falling back.
